items.title: Nordlys Labs
items.description: Checkpoint-based LLM router that separates labelled data, training and runtime model selection. I co-founded Nordlys Labs and led its AI routing work through May 2026.
items.longDescription:
## Problem

Different requests benefit from different models, but routing must be learned without putting training work in the request path.

## Implementation

The public package separates three interfaces: `Dataset` for labelled outcomes, `Trainer` for fitting and saving a checkpoint, and `Router` for loading that checkpoint and selecting a configured model at runtime. Model costs are explicit configuration.

## My contribution

I co-founded Nordlys Labs and led the AI routing work, connecting model selection with the Python backend and API. The linked repository is a team codebase and may contain changes made after my role ended in May 2026.

items.title: LLM Judge Audit
items.description: Audits LLM judges for position, length, self-preference and consistency failures. On 150 JudgeBench pairs, Ministral-8B fell from **0.61 raw accuracy to 0.12 correct in both answer orders**.
items.longDescription:
## Problem

A judge can agree with human labels for the wrong reason. Raw accuracy alone can hide position bias, invalid responses and unstable verdicts.

## Implementation

I built labelled-pair ingestion, probe execution, parsing, caching, cost controls and scorecard reporting. The tool supports position, length, self-preference and repeat-consistency probes, plus accuracy, Cohen's kappa and Wilson confidence intervals.

## Supported result

The published comparison ran baseline and position probes on 150 hard JudgeBench pairs across six self-hosted judges. Ministral-8B reported 0.61 raw accuracy, but only 0.12 accuracy when it had to be correct in both answer orders. The repository includes 132 offline tests and a scripted demonstration; those validate the tool, not the six-model GPU run.

items.title: KV Cache Optimization
items.description: Benchmarks KV-cache compression strategies and their quality trade-offs. Stratigraphic reported a **2.2× smaller analytical KV cache for +0.04 perplexity** on Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct.
items.longDescription:
## Problem

KV caches grow with sequence length. Reducing their storage is useful only when the resulting quality loss is measured correctly.

## Implementation

I implemented attention-layout comparisons, recurrent-state experiments and a benchmark covering FullKV, H2O, SnapKV, INT8, INT4 and Stratigraphic compression. Stratigraphic assigns per-head precision zones and keeps high-attention tokens as FP16 anchors.

## Supported result

The repository reports Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct on WikiText-2 and an A100: 11.18 perplexity versus 11.15 for FullKV, with 2.2× analytical KV-cache compression. A key debugging result was discovering that quantisation originally ran before RoPE and missed the representation the cache actually used; moving it post-RoPE exposed the real INT4 degradation.

The compression figure is an analytical cache estimate, not total GPU-memory reduction.

items.title: Git-RLMs
items.description: Repository-analysis agent that explores code and git history incrementally through a REPL. It provides **12 git-aware tools**, sub-model delegation, trajectory logs and hard cost budgets.
items.longDescription:
## Problem

Large repositories rarely fit usefully into one model context, and the relevant files or commits are not known in advance.

## Implementation

Git-RLM stores repository context outside the model and lets the model inspect it through an iterative Python REPL. Twelve tools cover logs, diffs, blame, historical file reads, code search, branches, tags and sub-model queries.

## Engineering controls

The CLI and Python API expose turn limits and dollar budgets, record the exploration trajectory, and support focused delegation to a cheaper sub-model. The result is an implementation of the Recursive Language Model pattern specialised for repository investigation.

items.title: Fracture
items.description: Internal-state fuzzing framework for LLM inference engines. It snapshots and mutates KV-cache, scheduler and prefix-cache state, then checks invariants through reusable oracles.
items.longDescription:
## Problem

Some inference-engine failures require rare internal states that are impractical to reach through API request fuzzing alone.

## Implementation

Fracture defines three engine-agnostic protocols: `Target` for snapshot, restore and stepping; `Mutator` for perturbing state; and `Oracle` for detecting invariant violations. A vLLM adapter connects the framework to a real serving engine.

## Evidence boundary

The upstream vLLM and SGLang issues linked in the repository motivate the state patterns Fracture targets. They are not presented as bugs personally discovered by this project. The portfolio therefore focuses on the implemented fuzzing architecture and reproducible snapshot-based workflow.

items.title: FinBalance
items.description: Synthetic month-end reconciliation benchmark with a deterministic ledger verifier, tool-using agent harness and hard gates for unauthorised accounting changes.
items.longDescription:
## Problem

A finance agent should be scored on whether its books reconcile, not on whether another language model likes its answer.

## Implementation

FinBalance generates synthetic company months with six discrepancy types, including a timing difference that must not be adjusted. Agents work through ledger and document tools; a double-entry replay engine checks balances, reconciliations and protected-account rules.

## Supported evidence

The benchmark includes Oracle, rule-based Baseline, Sloppy and Null agents to calibrate the metric, plus tests showing the generated gold corrections reconstruct clean balances across seeds. It is a synthetic reference implementation, not a production accounting system.

items.title: DuckBackflip
items.description: Simulation study of football and backflip behaviours for Open Duck Mini. A trained keep-up policy averaged **4.87 consecutive touches**; analysis showed why the current robot cannot backflip.
items.longDescription:
## Problem

Reward curves can make a simulated robot appear successful while contacts, unstable physics or falls produce the score.

## Implementation

I extended the Open Duck simulation with football and backflip tasks, sub-step contact detection, domain randomisation, PPO training, ONNX export checks and centroidal-momentum validation. The repository explicitly credits the upstream robot and base environments.

## Supported result

Across 128 deterministic simulated episodes, the keep-up policy averaged 4.87 consecutive touches, with a best of seven. A model-based momentum budget found only an 11% inertia reduction from tucking, making the required backflip jump unrealistic for the identified hobby servos. Everything is simulation-only; a successful backflip was not trained.

items.title: Field Report
items.description: Compares how Python libraries are documented with how they are used in public repositories. A reference run analysed **119 repositories and 544 call sites**.
items.longDescription:
## Problem

Documentation describes intended use, but maintainers also need evidence of real imports, call patterns and undocumented conventions.

## Implementation

Field Report discovers dependent repositories, verifies imports, extracts call sites, extracts canonical examples, compares both datasets and writes a Markdown report backed by SQLite. The same extractor handles source and documentation examples, so the comparison is structural rather than keyword-based.

## Supported result

For `clerk-backend-api`, the repository reports 119 importing repositories and 544 calls. It found five import paths for one options type and no use of the shipped retry configuration. Unresolved calls and failed searches remain visible instead of being silently counted as absence.

items.title: Altair
items.description: Browser-based 3D CSV explorer with on-device hand tracking. It renders a documented **2,200-point dataset in one instanced draw call** across three graph topologies.
items.longDescription:
## Problem

Tabular data can hide structure, while conventional charts make it difficult to move between alternative network views interactively.

## Implementation

Altair parses a CSV, maps numeric and categorical columns, optionally runs UMAP in a web worker, builds a nearest-neighbour graph and renders every point through one Three.js instanced mesh. MediaPipe classifies hand gestures locally in the browser; webcam frames are not uploaded.

## Supported evidence

The repository documents a captured 2,200-point dataset, three topology modes and gesture handling at roughly 30 fps. There is deliberately no hard-coded particle cap; practical scale is bounded by the JavaScript simulation loop.
